<div class="page-shell">

<header class="masthead">
  <div class="eyebrow">WebR practical</div>
  <h1>Interaction terms in regression</h1>
  <p>When the effect of one predictor depends on another, add an interaction. You will compare additive and interaction models, read group-specific slopes, and extend the idea to polytomous factors and two continuous predictors.</p>
</header>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Overview</h2>

An <strong>interaction</strong> means the effect of one predictor on the outcome <strong>depends on</strong> the level of another predictor.

Without an interaction, an <strong>additive</strong> model assumes that effect stays the same at every level of the other predictor. Fitted lines share the same slope and differ only in intercept.

With an interaction, different levels can have their own slope. The lines are no longer parallel.

In R, write an interaction with a colon:

```r
lm(outcome ~ x + group + x:group, data = my_data)
```

The shorthand `x * group` expands to `x + group + x:group`.

In this practical you will:

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li>Compare additive and interaction models with a binary predictor.</li>
  <li>Build slope-by-group tables from the coefficient output.</li>
  <li>Extend the same logic to a polytomous categorical predictor.</li>
  <li>Read a continuous-by-continuous interaction as a slope that changes with the second predictor.</li>
</ul>

After answering the questions, <strong>your completion code will be revealed.</strong>

</section>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 1</div>
  <p>An interaction model allows different groups to have different what?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="a">Sample sizes only.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="b">Slopes for the continuous predictor.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p0" value="c">P-values for the intercept only.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. The interaction lets the continuous slope change by group." data-incorrect="Not quite. The key change is that each group can get its own slope for the continuous predictor."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 1: Binary predictor and a continuous predictor</h2>

Question: does blood pressure medication change the BMI-to-systolic-BP relationship?

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li><strong>Outcome:</strong> <code>sysBP</code> (systolic blood pressure, mmHg)</li>
  <li><strong>Predictors:</strong> <code>BMI</code> and <code>BPmeds</code> (on medication or not; not on meds = reference)</li>
</ul>

We will fit three models:

<table class="coef-table">
  <tr><th>Model</th><th>R formula</th><th>What it allows</th></tr>
  <tr><td><strong>m1</strong></td><td><code>sysBP ~ BMI</code></td><td>One line for everyone</td></tr>
  <tr><td><strong>m2</strong></td><td><code>sysBP ~ BMI + BPmeds</code></td><td>Two parallel lines, same BMI slope</td></tr>
  <tr><td><strong>m3</strong></td><td><code>sysBP ~ BMI + BPmeds + BMI:BPmeds</code></td><td>Two lines, each with its own slope</td></tr>
</table>

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: create the blood pressure data</h3>

```{webr-r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(7)
n <- 180
bp_dat <- data.frame(
  BMI = runif(n, 20, 38),
  BPmeds = sample(c("not_on_meds", "on_meds"), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.55, 0.45))
)
bp_dat$sysBP <- with(
  bp_dat,
  87.64 + 1.70 * BMI +
    ifelse(BPmeds == "on_meds", 57.11 - 1.00 * BMI, 0) +
    rnorm(n, 0, 4)
)
bp_dat$BPmeds <- factor(bp_dat$BPmeds, levels = c("not_on_meds", "on_meds"))

head(bp_dat)
```

</div>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: additive model (m2) and interaction model (m3)</h3>

```{webr-r}
mod_add <- lm(sysBP ~ BMI + BPmeds, data = bp_dat)
mod_int <- lm(sysBP ~ BMI + BPmeds + BMI:BPmeds, data = bp_dat)

cat("--- Additive model ---\n")
summary(mod_add)

cat("\n--- Interaction model ---\n")
summary(mod_int)
```

</div>

```{=html}
<div class="svg-panel" aria-label="Parallel versus non-parallel group lines">
<svg viewBox="0 0 760 220" role="img">
  <rect width="760" height="220" rx="8" fill="#fff"/>
  <text x="190" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="800" fill="#173234">Additive: parallel lines</text>
  <line x1="30" y1="185" x2="350" y2="185" stroke="#5d7475" stroke-width="1.2"/>
  <line x1="30" y1="35" x2="30" y2="185" stroke="#5d7475" stroke-width="1.2"/>
  <line x1="45" y1="165" x2="335" y2="95" stroke="#2f5f98" stroke-width="2.2"/>
  <line x1="45" y1="125" x2="335" y2="55" stroke="#b83b5e" stroke-width="2.2"/>
  <text x="190" y="205" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" font-weight="700" fill="#5d7475">BMI</text>
  <text x="570" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="800" fill="#173234">Interaction: slopes differ</text>
  <line x1="410" y1="185" x2="730" y2="185" stroke="#5d7475" stroke-width="1.2"/>
  <line x1="410" y1="35" x2="410" y2="185" stroke="#5d7475" stroke-width="1.2"/>
  <line x1="425" y1="170" x2="715" y2="70" stroke="#2f5f98" stroke-width="2.2"/>
  <line x1="425" y1="110" x2="715" y2="82" stroke="#b83b5e" stroke-width="2.2"/>
  <text x="570" y="205" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" font-weight="700" fill="#5d7475">BMI</text>
  <text x="500" y="145" font-size="9.5" font-weight="800" fill="#2f5f98">not on meds</text>
  <text x="500" y="95" font-size="9.5" font-weight="800" fill="#b83b5e">on meds</text>
</svg>
<p class="svg-caption">Left: one shared BMI slope. Right: medication can change both the intercept gap and the BMI slope.</p>
</div>
```

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 2</div>
  <p>In the <strong>additive</strong> model, the BMI slope applies to:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="a">Both medication groups (one shared slope).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="b">Only people not on medication.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p1" value="c">Only people on medication.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Without an interaction, both groups share the same BMI coefficient." data-incorrect="Not quite. An additive model has a single BMI row that applies to everyone."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Slopes by group (interaction model)</h2>

Round your fitted coefficients to two decimals if needed. The pattern is always the same.

<p class="coef-key"><span class="c0">intercept</span> · <span class="c1">BMI</span> · <span class="c2">BPmeds</span> · <span class="c3">interaction</span></p>

<table class="coef-table">
  <tr><th>Group</th><th>Intercept</th><th>BMI slope</th></tr>
  <tr><td>Not on meds (reference)</td><td><span class="c0">b<sub>0</sub></span> from <code>(Intercept)</code></td><td><span class="c1">b<sub>1</sub></span> from plain <code>BMI</code> row</td></tr>
  <tr><td>On meds</td><td><span class="c0">b<sub>0</sub></span> + <span class="c2">b<sub>2</sub></span></td><td><span class="c1">b<sub>1</sub></span> + <span class="c3">b<sub>3</sub></span></td></tr>
</table>

<p>The reference group's slope is the plain <code>BMI</code> row alone. For the non-reference group, add the <code>BMI:BPmedson_meds</code> interaction row to that slope.</p>

<div class="formula-panel">

$$
\hat{y} = b_0 + b_1 x + b_2 g + b_3 (x \cdot g)
$$

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li><code>g = 0</code> for the reference group, <code>g = 1</code> for on meds.</li>
  <li><strong>Reference BMI slope</strong> = $b_1$.</li>
  <li><strong>Non-reference BMI slope</strong> = $b_1 + b_3$.</li>
</ul>

</div>

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: build the slope table from your model</h3>

```{webr-r}
b <- coef(mod_int)
b0 <- b["(Intercept)"]
b1 <- b["BMI"]
b2 <- b["BPmedson_meds"]
b3 <- b["BMI:BPmedson_meds"]

slope_table <- data.frame(
  group = c("Not on meds (ref)", "On meds"),
  intercept = c(b0, b0 + b2),
  BMI_slope = c(b1, b1 + b3)
)

round(slope_table, 2)
```

</div>

<label><input type="radio" name="p2" value="b"><code>BMI</code> + <code>BMI:BPmedson_meds</code> (about +0.7).</label>

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 5</div>
  <p>Which R formula adds the interaction between <code>BMI</code> and <code>BPmeds</code>?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p4" value="a"><code>lm(sysBP ~ BMI + BPmeds + BMI:BPmeds, data = bp_dat)</code></label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p4" value="b"><code>lm(sysBP ~ BMI + BPmeds - BMI:BPmeds, data = bp_dat)</code></label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p4" value="c"><code>lm(sysBP ~ BMI * BPmeds - BMI, data = bp_dat)</code></label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. The colon joins the two predictors into one interaction term." data-incorrect="Not quite. Write the two main effects plus BMI:BPmeds, or use BMI * BPmeds."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 2: Another binary example (education and sex)</h2>

Same pattern, different variables. Outcome: <code>wage</code> ($1000s per year). Predictors: <code>educ</code> (years) and <code>sex</code> (female = reference).

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: wage data and interaction model</h3>

```{webr-r}
set.seed(11)
wages <- data.frame(
  educ = sample(10:18, 120, replace = TRUE),
  sex = sample(c("female", "male"), 120, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.52, 0.48))
)
wages$wage <- with(
  wages,
  6.00 + 1.70 * educ + ifelse(sex == "male", 6.00 + 0.80 * educ, 0) + rnorm(120, 0, 2)
)
wages$sex <- factor(wages$sex, levels = c("female", "male"))

mod_wage <- lm(wage ~ educ + sex + educ:sex, data = wages)
summary(mod_wage)

b <- coef(mod_wage)
wage_table <- data.frame(
  group = c("Female (ref)", "Male"),
  intercept = c(b["(Intercept)"], b["(Intercept)"] + b["sexmale"]),
  educ_slope = c(b["educ"], b["educ"] + b["educ:sexmale"])
)
round(wage_table, 2)
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 6</div>
  <p>From the wage slope table, each extra year of education is associated with a wage gain of about:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p5" value="a">$1.7k for males and $1.7k for females (same slope).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p5" value="b">$2.5k for males and $1.7k for females.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p5" value="c">$0.8k for males and $1.7k for females.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Male educ slope = 1.70 + 0.80 ≈ 2.50; female stays at 1.70." data-incorrect="Not quite. The reference educ slope is 1.70; add educ:sexmale for males."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">

  <p>Predict wage for a male with 16 years of education (use rounded slope-table values):</p>

<label><input type="radio" name="p6" value="a">12.00 + 2.50 × 16 = 52</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p6" value="b">6.00 + 1.70 × 16 = 33.2</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p6" value="c">12.00 + 1.70 × 16 = 39.2</label>
  </div>

</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 3: Polytomous categorical predictor</h2>

With <strong>K</strong> levels, R still uses one reference level. You get <strong>K − 1</strong> dummy coefficients for the factor and <strong>K − 1</strong> interaction terms with the continuous predictor.

Example: birth weight (<code>bwt</code>, grams) from mother's pre-pregnancy weight (<code>lwt</code>, pounds) and race (<code>race</code>, three levels; white = reference).

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li>Reference group <strong>lwt slope</strong> = plain <code>lwt</code> row.</li>
  <li>Each non-reference level adds its own <code>lwt:race</code> row to that slope.</li>
</ul>

<table class="coef-table">
  <tr><th>Group</th><th>Intercept</th><th>lwt slope</th></tr>
  <tr><td>White (reference)</td><td><span class="c0">b<sub>0</sub></span></td><td><span class="c1">b<sub>lwt</sub></span></td></tr>
  <tr><td>Black</td><td><span class="c0">b<sub>0</sub></span> + <span class="c2">b<sub>black</sub></span></td><td><span class="c1">b<sub>lwt</sub></span> + <span class="c3">b<sub>lwt:black</sub></span></td></tr>
  <tr><td>Other</td><td><span class="c0">b<sub>0</sub></span> + <span class="c2">b<sub>other</sub></span></td><td><span class="c1">b<sub>lwt</sub></span> + <span class="c3">b<sub>lwt:other</sub></span></td></tr>
</table>

There is no separate interaction row for the reference level because it is absorbed into the main <code>lwt</code> effect.

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: birth weight, race, and lwt interaction</h3>

```{webr-r}
library(MASS)
data(birthwt)

bwt_dat <- birthwt |>
  mutate(race = factor(race,
                       levels = c(1, 2, 3),
                       labels = c("white", "black", "other")))

mod_race <- lm(bwt ~ lwt + race + lwt:race, data = bwt_dat)
summary(mod_race)

b <- coef(mod_race)
race_table <- data.frame(
  group = c("White (ref)", "Black", "Other"),
  intercept = c(
    b["(Intercept)"],
    b["(Intercept)"] + b["raceblack"],
    b["(Intercept)"] + b["raceother"]
  ),
  lwt_slope = c(
    b["lwt"],
    b["lwt"] + b["lwt:raceblack"],
    b["lwt"] + b["lwt:raceother"]
  )
)

round(race_table, 2)
```

</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 8</div>
  <p>A polytomous factor with <strong>3 levels</strong> paired with one continuous predictor produces how many <code>lwt:race</code> interaction coefficients?</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p7" value="a">3 (one per level).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p7" value="b">2 (K − 1, same as the factor dummies).</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p7" value="c">1 (always a single interaction).</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. The reference level has no interaction row; each other level gets one." data-incorrect="Not quite. With K levels you get K−1 interaction terms, matching the K−1 dummy coefficients."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="c">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 9</div>
  <p>In your fitted model, the <strong>black</strong> group's lwt slope equals:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p8" value="a">The <code>raceblack</code> row alone.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p8" value="b">The intercept plus <code>raceblack</code>.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p8" value="c">The plain <code>lwt</code> row plus <code>lwt:raceblack</code>.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Same rule as the binary case: reference slope plus that group's interaction row." data-incorrect="Not quite. The lwt slope for black mothers = lwt coefficient + lwt:raceblack."></div>
</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>Part 4: Two continuous predictors</h2>

When both predictors are continuous, the interaction works the same algebraically:

<div class="formula-panel">

$$
\hat{y} = b_0 + b_1 x + b_2 z + b_3 (x \cdot z)
$$

<p>The slope of <strong>x</strong> depends on the value of <strong>z</strong>:</p>

$$
\text{slope of } x \text{ at a fixed } z = b_1 + b_3 z
$$

</div>

Instead of a group table, use a <strong>conditional slope table</strong> at chosen values of the second predictor:

<table class="coef-table">
  <tr><th>Value of <code>age</code> (hold <code>lwt</code> in model)</th><th>Slope of <code>lwt</code> on <code>bwt</code></th></tr>
  <tr><td>20 years</td><td><span class="c1">b<sub>lwt</sub></span> + 20 × <span class="c3">b<sub>lwt:age</sub></span></td></tr>
  <tr><td>25 years</td><td><span class="c1">b<sub>lwt</sub></span> + 25 × <span class="c3">b<sub>lwt:age</sub></span></td></tr>
  <tr><td>30 years</td><td><span class="c1">b<sub>lwt</sub></span> + 30 × <span class="c3">b<sub>lwt:age</sub></span></td></tr>
</table>

<p>At <code>age = 0</code> (often outside the data), the slope of <code>lwt</code> would equal the plain <code>lwt</code> row alone. In practice, pick meaningful values of the moderator.</p>

</section>

<div class="webr-wrap">

<h3>R code: continuous-by-continuous interaction</h3>

Replace each `____` with the correct variable name, then run the cell.

```{webr-r}
mod_cont <- lm(bwt ~ ____ + ____ + ____:____, data = bwt_dat)
summary(mod_cont)

b <- coef(mod_cont)
cond_slopes <- data.frame(
  age = c(20, 25, 30),
  lwt_slope = b["lwt"] + c(20, 25, 30) * b["lwt:age"]
)
round(cond_slopes, 2)
```

</div>

<details class="answer">
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

```r
mod_cont <- lm(bwt ~ lwt + age + lwt:age, data = bwt_dat)
```

The plain `lwt` row is the lwt slope when age = 0. At age = 25, add 25 × `lwt:age`.

</details>

<div class="practice" data-answer="b">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 10</div>
  <p>Using rounded coefficients from your fitted model (about <code>lwt</code> = +11.3 and <code>lwt:age</code> = −0.30), the slope of lwt on birth weight at age = 25 is about:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p9" value="a">11.3 − 0.30 = 11.0</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p9" value="b">11.3 + 25 × (−0.30) = 3.8</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p9" value="c">11.3 + (−0.30) = 11.0</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Multiply the interaction by the moderator value, then add to the main lwt slope." data-incorrect="Not quite. Use lwt coefficient + age × lwt:age = 11.3 + 25(−0.30)."></div>
</div>

<div class="practice" data-answer="a">
  <div class="practice-title">Question 11</div>
  <p>A continuous-by-continuous interaction means:</p>
  <div class="choice-set">
<label><input type="radio" name="p10" value="a">The effect of one continuous predictor changes across values of the other.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p10" value="b">Both predictors must be converted to factors first.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p10" value="c">The model cannot include an intercept.</label>
  </div>

</div>

<section class="panel">

<h2>When to fit an interaction</h2>

<div class="callout warning">

<ul class="tight-list">
  <li>Fit one when it is <strong>well established</strong> in the literature or is your <strong>research question</strong> (does X's effect on Y depend on Z?).</li>
  <li>Biology or study design may strongly suggest <strong>effect modification</strong>.</li>
  <li>Otherwise default to an <strong>additive</strong> model: easier to read and often more stable.</li>
  <li>Do <strong>not</strong> fit all pairwise interactions and keep only significant ones. That is p-hacking and invalidates those p-values.</li>
</ul>

</div>

</section>

<div class="practice" data-answer="c">

<label><input type="radio" name="p11" value="a">It makes every model R-squared as large as possible, regardless of theory.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p11" value="b">You tried several interactions and kept only those with p &lt; 0.05.</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="p11" value="c">You want to test whether the BMI effect on sysBP differs by medication status.</label>
  </div>
  <button type="button">Check</button>
  <div class="practice-feedback" data-correct="Correct. Interactions should be planned, not cherry-picked after screening many models." data-incorrect="Not quite. A pre-specified research question or known effect modification is the right motivation."></div>
</div>

<script>
const COMPLETION_CODE = "INTMOD7X";
const COMPLETION_REQUIRED = 10;

function updateCompletion() {
  const cards = document.querySelectorAll(".practice");
  const correct = document.querySelectorAll(".practice.is-correct").length;
  const total = cards.length;
  const progress = document.getElementById("code-progress");
  const box = document.getElementById("code-box");
  const value = document.getElementById("code-value");

  if (progress) {
    progress.textContent = correct + " of " + total + " correct (need at least " + COMPLETION_REQUIRED + ")";
  }

  if (box && value) {
    if (correct >= COMPLETION_REQUIRED) {
      value.textContent = COMPLETION_CODE;
      box.style.display = "block";
    } else {
      box.style.display = "none";
    }
  }
}

document.querySelectorAll(".practice").forEach((card) => {
  const button = card.querySelector("button");
  const feedback = card.querySelector(".practice-feedback");
  const answer = card.dataset.answer;

  button.addEventListener("click", () => {
    const selected = card.querySelector("input[type='radio']:checked");
    card.classList.remove("is-correct", "is-incorrect");
    card.querySelectorAll("label").forEach((label) => {
      label.classList.remove("correct-choice", "incorrect-choice");
    });

    if (!selected) {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      feedback.textContent = "Choose an answer first, then check it.";
      updateCompletion();
      return;
    }

    const selectedLabel = selected.closest("label");
    const correctInput = card.querySelector(`input[value="${answer}"]`);
    const correctLabel = correctInput ? correctInput.closest("label") : null;

    if (selected.value === answer) {
      card.classList.add("is-correct");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.correct;
    } else {
      card.classList.add("is-incorrect");
      selectedLabel.classList.add("incorrect-choice");
      if (correctLabel) correctLabel.classList.add("correct-choice");
      feedback.textContent = feedback.dataset.incorrect;
    }

    updateCompletion();
  });
});

updateCompletion();
</script>
